page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.6xlarge is a storage-dense server instance belonging to the ecs.d1 family. It is equipped with 24 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The server incorporates 96.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Virtualization is managed via the KVM hypervisor.

A key defining hardware feature of the ecs.d1.6xlarge is its integrated local storage array, providing 70,866 GB of capacity delivered on local hard disk drives (HDDs). Network throughput is supported by an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile. No dedicated GPUs are included in this instance configuration.

By coupling large magnetic storage density with moderate compute resources and dedicated vCPUs, the server provides high capacity per node for bulk storage tasks where raw HDD throughput is required. The reliance on magnetic HDD storage rather than NVMe SSDs introduces IOPS and latency tradeoffs for random I/O workloads. The configuration is suited for big data processing, distributed file systems, data archiving, log analysis, and large-scale data warehousing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.6xlarge is a storage-dense x86_64 server instance provisioned on KVM hypervisors. Powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, the instance features 24 dedicated vCPUs and 96.0 GB of memory, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The primary hardware highlight is its bundled local storage array comprising 70,866 GB of hard disk drive (HDD) capacity. Network connectivity is backed by an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth. While the mechanical HDD storage profile presents higher latency and lower random I/O throughput relative to modern solid-state options, it provides efficient cost density for throughput-oriented bulk storage requirements. The ecs.d1.6xlarge is structured for data-intensive applications, including distributed file systems, batch log analysis, data lakes, and cold or warm archive repositories.
